{{recipesummary|category=Beef recipes|servings=4|time=1 hour|difficulty=2}}
{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Meat_Recipes|Meat recipes]]

'''Hamburger deluxe''' turns a hamburger into a whole new experience. This recipe evolved over a couple of decades with ingredients being added or deleted as tastes changed. 

==Ingredients==

=== Hamburgers ===
*¾ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (350 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) lean ground [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]]
*¼ lb (110 g) ground [[Cookbook:Lamb|lamb]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (125 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Oats|rolled oats]]
*2 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] (15 [[Cookbook:ML|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Grape Seed Oil|grapeseed oil]] (or other lightly flavoured [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]])
*1 tablespoon (15 ml) [[Cookbook:Dijon Mustard|Dijon mustard]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (5 g) ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
*½ teaspoon (2 ml) [[Cookbook:Worcestershire Sauce|Worcestershire Sauce]]
*1 tablespoon (15 ml) chipotle [[Cookbook:Barbecue Sauce|BBQ Sauce]], or a healthy [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Chili Pepper|chipotle powder]]
*½ teaspoon (2–3 g) [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

=== Topping ===
*[[Cookbook:Cheese|Cheese]], smoked [[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|cheddar]] is best, but any cheddar or your favourite cheese will do
*[[Cookbook:Sour Cream|Sour cream]]
*Plain [[Cookbook:Cream Cheese|cream cheese]], sliced thinly
*1 Vidalia [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], coarsely chopped (Spanish onion will do)
*¼ pound (110 g) button [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]], sliced thin
*1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* Fresh ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]] to taste
*Favourite hamburger condiments
*4 hamburger buns

==Special equipment==
*[[Cookbook:Grill|Grill]]

==Procedure==
#[[Cookbook:Sautéing|Sauté]] onions and mushrooms in butter until lightly brown, then set aside.
#Mix all of the hamburger ingredients together until well-mixed, and let rest for 15 minutes.
#Heat grill to medium-high.
#Divide hamburger mix into 4 equal balls.
#Form patties by slapping the burgers back and forth from one palm to the other until they are about an inch thick.
#[[Cookbook:Grilling|Grill]] burgers to desired [[Cookbook:Meat and Poultry#Doneness|doneness]], turning every few minutes and adding cheese after the last flipping of the burgers
#Serve on the buns, with the onion/mushroom mixture, a dollop of sour cream, and a thin slice of cream cheese.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* The suggestion to flip the meat a number of times comes from a book concerning the science of cooking. The theory is that the juices in meat rise to the surface of the meat and are then lost during grilling. By turning the meat regularly, you reduce the capacity of the juices to rise out of, and run off, the meat.
* The egg and oats combine to bind the hamburgers and help prevent them from falling apart on the grill.
